titre: The Shrek Toaster Is the Only Black Friday Deal You Need
extrait: Do you ever throw some bread in the toaster and think to yourself, "Wow, this toast would taste better with Shrek’s face on it?" Well, Amazon’s Black Friday deals can make your questionable culinary dream a reality. Uncanny Brands produces a line of retro TV-themed toasters that burn images straight onto your bread. For the season of deals, Amazon gave most of these quirky (and, somehow, officially licensed) toasters a 15% discount, bringing them to their lowest-ever prices. Amazon’s discount knocks around $7 off the price of each toaster in these lightning deals, which will disappear once they’re fully claimed. For whatever reason, that seems to be happening surprisingly fast. The list of themed toasters is about as weird as the concept itself. We’ve got Shrek, of course, but you can also sear into your bread images of Bluey, Sonic, Snoopy, and, um, Bob Ross? Uncanny Valley also produces a Grinch toaster, but that one isn't getting a discount. Stingy guy, I guess. According to the official listing, the two-slot toaster features an adjustable thermostat with defrost, quick stop, and reheat functions. Each toaster is emblazoned with an image, dedicated to whatever weird property it prints on bread, in a light-up frame. I’m going to be honest, I can’t vouch for the quality of the Shrek toaster myself. I use the cheapest possible toaster option from Amazon and have been pretty satisfied with it. Still, maybe I’m not quite as satisfied as users of the Shrek-ster: "I love this toaster," says the most-upvoted review. "I like that it lights up when you are making toast." Very insightful, I know. The most legit-looking reviews note that you have to do a little experimentation to find the right settings for maximum image effect, and sometimes that means straight-up burning the bread. Apparently you might also notice a weird smell the first time you use it. Yum! We’re in the thick of Black Friday season. For the Shrek-maxxers, you can probably find the movie in Amazon’s DVD and Blu-ray deals, while Dreamworks home Peacock is one of the many services offering a Black Friday streaming discount. Even LEGO Shrek is on sale in the mess of LEGO deals. If you’re looking for somewhat normal deals, we’ve got you covered there, too. Check out what’s happening at Nintendo, PlayStation, and Xbox, or our full guide to all things Black Friday. titre: The Lego Minifigures Shrek series are discounted for Black Friday
chapo: The Lego Minifigures Shrek Series is down 30% at the Lego website, in a deal I've been waiting months for, with Black Friday deals on single and 6-packs.

I'd never paid much mind to the Lego Minifigures Series, but the September release of the Shrek series changed all of that. One of the load-bearing icons of Zillennial culture has been Lego-ified, and I've been slowly collecting the figures ever since. I shouldn't have, though, as a Black Friday discount means I should have waited. You can now pick up the Minifigures Shrek Series boxes for 30% off at the Lego website, so the packs are $3.49 in the US and £2.44 in the UK, and in the US the 6-pack box is also down to $20. With 12 figures to collect, a 30% saving gets you 12 boxes for the price of 9 (although Minifigures are random, and by the way my own collection is going, I'm going to need far more than 12 boxes to bag them all). It's certainly one of the stronger Lego Black Friday deals so far. As far as I can tell, this is the only price reduction the Lego Minifigures Shrek Series has seen. Given that the series is due to wrap up in the next few months, it's time to start buying if you haven't already. This six-pack doesn't actually save you money over buying six individual packs, but it's a better gift-sized pack if you're buying for someone else. And rolling six dice at once feels luckier than one die six times, right? Don't want a minifigure, but a massive-figure? The Lego Shrek building kit, which makes a statue of Shrek and Donkey (and has a Puss in Boots minifigure) is reduced in the Black Friday sales too. It's not as cute as the figs, but it's a better build (and isn't as weird-looking as whatever we're getting in Shrek 5!). This Shrek building kit is enjoying its first serious discount, making for a 20% saving in total. It's not a play kit but a model which you'll put on a shelf or cupboard. Not all brands are reducing this kit just yet, and Amazon has one of the few reductions. When the Lego Minifigures Shrek series was announced, I knew I could very quickly spend too much money on these boxes.
